basis: Dural vascular malformation; hydrocephalus and CNS cysts occur in 30-79%. Damaging ocular findings are under 30%; tinnitus alone does not establish ear damage.
Cerebellar, retinal and renal disease define this subtype; hepatic fibrosis in 5/5 and cirrhosis in 3/4 support hepatic involvement.
Benign papillary neoplasm arising in the bronchial epithelium.
Tumour of pancreatic endocrine lineage, despite absence of a hormone-related syndrome; exocrine pancreatic damage is not defining.
Nonsyndromic progressive sensorineural hearing loss.
Neuronal lysosomal storage disorder; visual impairment in 2/2, retinal dystrophy in 1/2 and optic atrophy in 1/1 support ocular involvement.
Defined by developmental language impairment, childhood speech apraxia and intellectual disability; additional joint findings lack a qualifying frequency.
Dysplastic glandular neoplasm originating in rectal mucosa.
Inherited cerebral photosensitivity classified under photosensitive epilepsy; light triggering does not imply ocular disease.
Combined immunodeficiency with defining T-cell lymphopenia in 5/5. Recurrent respiratory infections are separate diseases; diarrhea alone does not establish intestinal damage.
Parasitic larval infection; hepatic, pulmonary and ocular injury varies across clinical forms and is not established in at least 30% across this umbrella.
Usher type 1 is defined by congenital sensorineural deafness, vestibular dysfunction and progressive retinal degeneration.
Congenital keratinization disorder; structural eyelid involvement with ectropion in 16/17 supports ocular involvement. Contractures occur in under 30%.
Inherited cortisol-regeneration defect causing adrenal androgen excess; hirsutism is a hormonal manifestation rather than destructive skin disease.
Broad sex-chromosome anomaly group; gonadal endocrine dysfunction is a major shared manifestation. Other organ abnormalities vary substantially by karyotype.
PLG-related bradykinin angioedema characteristically affects facial subcutis, lips and tongue/oral mucosa. Immune mediation and common laryngeal injury are not established.
Spinal motor-neuron disease with defining congenital joint contractures and muscle atrophy.
Hereditary juvenile open-angle glaucoma with optic nerve damage.
Disorder of phagocytic immune-cell function; blood-cell and immune axes apply. Tissue infiltration and organ injury are subtype-dependent.
Hyperplasia of urinary tract urothelium; the renal axis includes the entire urinary tract.
Photosensitive brittle-hair and skin disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment affects roughly 80%. Damaging ocular findings are not clearly at least 30%; infections are separate diseases.
Systemic hypertension defines the disease; the underlying cause and separately diagnosed organ complications are not inherent additional axes.
Congenital persistence of the ductus arteriosus, documented in 6/6 patients.
Thyrotropin-producing carcinoma originates in the pituitary endocrine gland; additional damaging organ involvement is not established as common.
Thoracic skeletal malformation supports musculoskeletal labeling; detailed phenotype and frequencies are unavailable. Facial and genital anomalies alone establish no additional axis.
